input.claim_text: On 3 February 2023 heavy rain caused the creek behind our property to overflow and water came into our home, ruining the carpets in the living room and soaking the bottom of the plasterboard walls. It happened really fast, within about an hour the water was ankle deep inside. We've had to rip up the carpet already because it started smelling. I think it'll cost around $9,000 to fix the flooring and walls.

output.cause: creek overflowed due to heavy rain
output.damaged_item: living room carpets and plasterboard walls

input.query: Is flood damage from creek overflow covered?

output.answer: I don't have enough information to answer that -- no matching policy text was found.

input.query: flood definition coverage rising water creek river overflow exclusion

turns.text:
DECISION: approve

Reasoning: The claim involves water entering the home due to a creek overflowing after heavy rain, which matches RAA's policy definition of "Flood" — "the covering of normally dry land by water that has escaped ... from any river, creek or other natural watercourse" (RAA Contents PDS, p.87). None of the listed flood exclusions apply here (the damage is not to unbuilt structures, pools, tanks, paint-only, driveways, or from actions of the sea) — the loss is to living room carpet and plasterboard walls, which is standard coverable flood damage (RAA Contents PDS, p.50, 87-88).

The policyholder's certificate shows an excess of $500 and a coverage limit of $45,000, well above the claimed $9,000. Applying the excess: payout = $9,000 - $500 = $8,500.

Final payout: $8,500, approved under the Flood section of the RAA Home/Contents policy.
